title: A Workflow of Sonnet agents merges combined PRs pairwise on dry trees round by round while CI runs; the real PR is built once from the last round
why: Owner idea 21:45 CST Nov 13, in runner 10's chat (relayed by the consultant): combine the merge queues further and further while a run is already in CI, instead of one big serial queue.
source: Consultant 21:46 CST Nov 13, relaying runner 10 relaying the owner.
note: Triage 21:46 CST Nov 13: under step batch-runner-scales. Shape per the consultant: a Workflow of Sonnet agents takes two large combined PRs each, merges them pairwise on dry trees (no push), round by round (8 combine to 4, then further) while CI runs; a clashing member leaves by name to its lane; the real PR is built from the last round on the newest main, linted once, one CI run. Runner 10 runs it (its Workflow grant, ruling own-runner-workflow-optin, covers Sonnet agents); the coordinator tracks. Merges stay serial. Nothing here is measured: the number of rounds, the clash rate (runner 10's dry runs found 46 of 62 members clean for combine-m2, 17 of 990 pairs clashing in set 1) and the time saved are unmeasured by triage.
